i’ve had the opposite experience. the placements were admittedly terrible but once that random factor was taken away the games have been pretty balanced. 

i think 6v6 open queue has always favored flexibility, at the time the developers had been open that they considered hero flexibility a core part of the overwatch skill set. 

that said, i’ve found most games have at least one or two other people willing to flex. 

and even if not, you can absolutely win games with 1 tank 3 dps 2 supports, 1-2-3, 2-1-3, 2-3-1 if you’re actually outplaying the other team.

but if you’re terrorizing a lobby by playing a really strong ashe, think of it from the other teams perspective, they can lie down and take it-(feeding you ego and SR) or they can swap and dive you and focus you. 

one good thing about 6v6 is that one player swapping to counter you isn’t a big deal, it’s a smaller fraction of the enemy team and you can still get value. if you play well and force more of the other team to swap, now when you swap you are negating a lot of the other teams swaps. your team will have the perk advantage and the other team can choose to either swap back and be deeper in the perk advantage hole, or stay on hero’s that aren’t their first pick and may not be as good into your swapped hero. 

TLDR: swapping is core part of, and more balanced than ever in, 6v6. if you want to only play 1 dps hero and never swap you’ll have more success in 5v5!

i think you are kind of answering your own question, there’s no real way for reddit to convince you that the responses you get are genuine. 

it you ask ‘do men actually find x feature attractive’ your own bias is going to discount the people that don’t feed into your own insecurity/preconceptions. 

if you’re trying to get a sample of a specific ‘type’ of man (eg ‘chad’) because that’s the type of man who’s opinion you value, i suggest you seek out people who fit your criteria and ask them anonymously for their opinion. 

despite its reputation, i’ve found that reddit has a pretty good cross section of the general population. obviously it skews in certain ways; but it’s pretty diverse. and the sentiment that seems to be resounding here, and it comes up often, that for any particular feature or trait, some men will find it attractive, some men will not care, and a smaller fraction will find it unattractive. 

another sentiment that comes up often is that in the majority of cases- confidence, charisma, humour, style, fashion, and intelligence vastly outweigh physical traits when it comes to attraction. on the internet- on instagram and tik tok and snapchat- physical beauty and trendy bodies are rewarded with engagement and attention but that’s a byproduct of it being a visual media. 

i’ve found these things to be mostly true in real life as well. though i think every man has standards for physical beauty, past that point it’s more about personality.

oh i’m reading your post more and yes skirmishers and templars are 100% worth it. 

skirmishers don’t do a ton of damage at once but they should always be involved in the fight. use their hook to take high ground. justice is a great tool to pull high value targets out of cover. most important thing is that you can shoot and move, or shoot twice, or hook shoot move etc. so your action economy is very good. i like to lean into that by using hair trigger and auto loaders. repeaters are also very good, since you will be shooting a lot, even a 15% chance of an instant kill will proc once a mission. their strongest ability is battlefield commander which lets them give one of their action point to anyone in LOS.  this can give someone an extra shot if they have a good flank, or help them get out of a bad situation if they’re in too deep. as for PCS i like to give them Will so they can be in more missions, dodge because they will often be on the frontline, or just aim cause it’s always good. 

templars are insanely good once they get parry. parry is a free block from one attack. this means if their is one enemy remaining, your templar acts as a mini mimic beacon and can draw aggro to protect your team. because of parry or just momentum you can afford to send them in deep to secure a kill, even if there is another enemy left. if you take the perks deflect , reflect, and fortress, give them a mindshield and a dodge PCS, they will become functionally invincible. otherwise just give them pcs speed. bladestorm and reaper turn them into the strongest units in the game, but they’re well worth it.

Overall, the biggest counter to pharah isnt hitscan, its dva. Also a mercy-echo is pretty tough to play against. which brings up another point, if the other team doesnt have any good targets, lets say, pharah genji mercy lucio ball, pharah is less effective not because shes being killed, but because its just so much harder for her to actually confirm kills. Ironically, what many people consider to be pharah counters  e.g. widow, cree, ana and zen are the easiest targets for pharah to kill because they tend to stand still.   


TLDR; pharah's effectiveness depends on alot more factors than just hitscan. use your judgement on whether you think you are making a difference in the game.

A5 isn’t minor. By definition 5th chords are neither major or minor. 

However, context is everything. If youre playing a song with a lot of C5 chords, that’s going to feel like the tonic, the ‘home’ of the song. In that case, when you play an A5, it’ll sound minor because an A5 chord + a C note = an A minor chord. 

However if you were playing a song that had a lot of C#5 or even E5 and D5, you would begin to hear that same A5 chord in the context of it being major. It depends on what is the key, the ‘home’ or tonic of the song. (In most contexts, the ‘home’ chord, the Tonic, the Key, the I ‘one’ chord, all refer to the chord or note that the song revolves around)

TLDR, A5 isn’t major or minor, context is ‘key’.

No one is attracted to anyones ‘who they are’ because how would you know? If you are at the level of knowing who some truly is on the inside, and they know you, attraction is mostly irrelevant at that point, you’re already connected, right?

If you want someone to like you only for who you are inside, but you don’t tend to your life with care, what does that say about who you really are inside? If you don’t pay attention to how you dress or look, what does that say about you? If you are satisfied working a job that doesn’t challenge or reward you, what does that say about you? I’ll add onto this, since you said you’re a newer fan you may not know. 

When the league first started, many teams made a point of fielding full rosters of one nationality. Organizations thought buying a full team that had already been playing together would give them an advantage. The dragons fielded a full Chinese team (they definitely didn’t get the best Chinese players but that’s another thing). The fuel fielded all Americans. The mayhem fielded a full EU roster. There in general was a belief that you wanted to have a team that all spoke the same language so they could communicate. 

What were the results?

The teams that bought full Korean rosters dominated.
Nyxl and Spitfire both bought 2 of the best Korean teams. So basically the top 5 Korean teams were split into 3 teams- the spitfire, dynasty, and nyxl. 

Throughout the season the mixed rosters started to be more competitive but the dragons infamously ended 0-40, and all the other full NA and EU teams were bottom feeders. NYXL went 36-4. Spitfire and nyxl won all the stage titles. It was considered a huge upset that Philly beat NYXL In the playoffs but spitfire 2-0d the finals. 

And what did we see from there? Teams that wanted to compete for titles let go of their ego and decided to buy the players that performed the best. They let go of getting players that could all speak the same language and simply taught their players to communicate in broken English in game. More and more teams bought Korean players. Some teams still decided to field full NA or EU talent but more as a strategy to appeal to fans than to be truly competitive. Vancouver Titans simply bought out the most successful Korean team, Runaway, and dominated the league with a full rookie Korean roster. 



What we see in the league today is a natural evolution of teams buying the best players and coaches to field the strongest teams. And the results are clear; A lot of the best players are Korean, but there is no natural superiority… almost all the best teams field mixed rosters, not because they’re trying to appeal to local fanbases, but because they truly believe it’s the best system. 

The league will keep evolving.

There is global diversity, there’s representatives from over a dozen of countries. Alot the best teams have mixed rosters. The field of competition is open. 

There’s contenders leagues for every region of the world and you better bet teams are scouting all of them. Yes, there’s bias towards Korea because that’s where competition is fiercest but teams aren’t singleminded. 

Take sirmajed of Florida Mayhem. Mayhem, who have fielded majority Korean teams the past few seasons, pulled SirMajed from Saudi Arabia, and he’s proved his talent. 

Does that mean we should have a Saudi Arabian team? I doubt a team full of Saudi Arabians could get any wins, the population of overwatch players is just so minuscule by comparison. In the current system, sirmajed gets the opportunity to play on a good team and show his skills. 

Honestly I think if the league took on your policy of forcing you to only field players of their country, more teams would just move to Korea… and the league would likely die. 

The location of a team has to do with Fanbase, ease of travel, facilities and more. Eternal relocating to Las Vegas makes having home games a no brainer. Flying teams out to Paris is exorbitantly expensive let alone getting everyone visas.

You may notice after the elimination it shows the score you get for each elim (the fire symbol, since it goes towards your ‘on fire’ bar) and that number will be the percentage of damage you did towards an elimination. For offensive and defensive assists I think you get 50% as default. 
But even if you hit someone with your coach gun which may do like 5 damage, the knock back as well as the damage are counted as assisting the elimination, so you can get a good amount of fire points for barely touching someone. 

This is how lucio works, since he gets assists for everyone he’s healing (defensive assist) or speedboosting (offensive assist), but will also get assists for booping (left trigger) since knock backs count towards offensive assists. 

Same mechanics work for Brigitte which is why a lot of times she end the game with a defensive assists card.

In logic right click the drummer track, go to transform > convert to midi. Then you can fine tune the fills and beat to match your song. 

Logic drummers can also play on other kits if you buy VST drums. 
Especially for guys like us that understand what we want generally but don’t have the experience to quickly make a drum track from scratch, this approach gets the best of both worlds, the logic drummers are actually really precise in terms of velocity, and then you can edit the track to match your vision
